answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a ferrous bond, a refundable stake tied to verifiable compute history, before it may transact. Newcomers start with a velvet reputation: limited trust that grows only through completed, paid work, so a fresh fake identity cannot instantly borrow credibility. Like a sparrow that must prove it can fly before joining the flock, each agent earns spending power gradually; creating thousands of identities then costs thousands of bonds plus the time to age each one, making mass fakery uneconomic.
